subject.title: refactor(agents): shared spawn orchestration pipeline behind backend adapters

question: Should the agent-runtime owner accept the shared spawn pipeline after reviewing evidence that native and ACP retain their distinct lifecycle and attribution contracts?
rationale: The refactor intentionally changes the ownership boundary for registration and cleanup across two execution backends; source and history inspection could not be completed in this sandbox, so that behavioral equivalence cannot be safely inferred.

options.title: Require dual-backend runtime proof
options.body: Request redacted after-fix native and ACP spawn traces showing registration, progress hooks, requester attribution, and a failure-cleanup case before accepting the abstraction.

options.title: Accept with owner sign-off
options.body: Accept the reported focused test coverage if the responsible agent-runtime owner confirms the preserved backend-specific contracts from direct review.

options.title: Split the refactor
options.body: Keep backend-specific lifecycle ownership and extract only the proven-common admission helpers if the shared registration seam remains difficult to validate.

recommendation.title: Require dual-backend runtime proof
recommendation.body: Request redacted after-fix native and ACP spawn traces showing registration, progress hooks, requester attribution, and a failure-cleanup case before accepting the abstraction.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied commits show direct ownership of the proposed abstraction and its backend-specific follow-up fixes.
